_about: WORDS THREE, HIS HOMEWORK, SHEET THREE: THE MOUTHS NOBODY HAS ASKED YET (VAMILY rules 454(c), 455, 461; ask rows 629, 637). Twelve cards, one screen of the tab, queued BEHIND sheet two so he never runs out. Sheets one and two asked 32 lines; these twelve are the places those never reached: the askers who send him after a boss (the mouth furthest from page one, 12 of 60 scary first), a middle-aged man (nobody between his kid and his old woman has been answered), the line with no mouth (what comes back after a choice: 231 of them), HIS OWN words on a button, an eerie post (is eerie his scary? it decides a quarter of the count), a loss, a real place, a sign read out, a man talked about on his card, his men outnumbered, a thank-you for help nobody paid for, and a second job giver beside the old woman he starred. tools/bohemia_words_two_homework.js reads every line out of the named file; nothing here is a line. No rewrite of ours rides on any card.
said: you show me one sentence or one dialog caption that you made and then I'll tell you how I want that shit to sound

cards.who_plain: A trucker with no truck, a grown man in the middle of his life
cards.when: he stops you to send you after the boss who sells the only map of the valley
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card that starts a boss's trail
cards.teaches: THE ASKER WHO SENDS YOU AFTER A BOSS, the mouth furthest from page one (12 of 60 lines scary first); and AGE: a grown man between his kid and his old woman; is losing his work his hell, and does he offer anything

cards.mouth: YOUR MAN, BEFORE A FIGHT WITH ANIMALS
cards.role: says why the animals are coming
cards.when: lab animals come at your crew on the road and the fight opens
cards.where: on the card that opens a FIGHT
cards.teaches: WHY THE ANIMALS ATTACK (your 11/14 ask: 'why the fuck the animals are attacking you') said by your own man, and WHAT YOUR MEN CALL YOU: the game fills in 'boss' (slices/bohemia_fight_why.js); is 'boss' right

cards.mouth: A ROAD STOP: WHAT COMES BACK
cards.role: the card answers after you pick 'Carry him to the nearest town.'
cards.who_plain: Nobody: the card itself, under the sick man's face
cards.when: you carried a sick stranger to the nearest town
cards.where: on the MAP, on the road card, after you pick
cards.teaches: THE LINE WITH NO MOUTH: 231 lines come back after a choice and about half are told, not said, yet they sit under a person's face; who should say this: him, one of your men, or nobody

cards.role: your answer, a button under his card
cards.to: one of your men, who just asked to leave and go to his mother and two sisters
cards.when: a man at the fire says the wells went dry on his family's street and he has to go to them
cards.where: on the MAP, the third button under a card at the night stop
cards.teaches: YOUR OWN VOICE: the first card about what YOU say. Nearly all of your 200 buttons are written like this, as a thing you do ('Say...'); a handful are in your own mouth ('Not our fight.', 'Forget it. We have work.'); which should a button be, and how hard is your boss voice

cards.when: it is a quiet day and she posts about what is still running up the road
cards.expect: the data center up the road
cards.teaches: IS EERIE SCARY? Nobody's body is in danger in this post, only something wrong that nobody can explain. 90 of the 349 lines we count as scary first are this kind and none of your four lines is; your answer decides whether they count

cards.who_plain: The oldest man in your crew, still standing
cards.when: you LOSE a fight and the ones left get up off the ground
cards.where: on the screen after a FIGHT you lost
cards.teaches: A LOSS: every card so far was a win or a talk; this is the worst moment the crew lives through and it is three short sentences, two of them orders

cards.who_plain: The last teller at the bank on Fourth Street
cards.when: you walk into the bank, where the money nobody wants is still in the cages
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card of a real place you visit
cards.teaches: THE LONGEST MOUTH: a real place's keeper talks for nine sentences about the dead dollar, the heart of the game (an economic crash); how long may a person talk, and is the money dying scary or funny

cards.role: reads out a flyer stapled to a pole
cards.who_plain: One of your own men, reading out the flyer the boss called THE POT put up, and what somebody wrote under it
cards.when: you go and look at the flyer a hungry cook told you about
cards.where: on the MAP, on the card of the thing that leads to a boss
cards.teaches: WRITTEN WORDS, READ OUT: a flyer and a scrawl under it, read by one of your men (the game never lets you speak for the valley); how should a sign in hell read, and how does your man read it to you

cards.role: the line under his name, about his past
cards.who_plain: Nobody says it: one line about your man, on his card
cards.when: you open the card of a man who was a thief before he joined you
cards.where: on the crew screen, on his card
cards.teaches: A MAN TALKED ABOUT, NOT TALKING: every man's card has one line of his past in the third person; who is saying it (him, the crew, nobody), and how much of his hell goes in it

cards.who_plain: The man in your crew who prays
cards.when: the fight opens and there are a lot more of them than of you
cards.where: in a FIGHT, over his head
cards.teaches: THE MOST SCARED SECOND OF A FIGHT, from a man of God: does a praying man swear when he is this scared (your 10/24 ask: 'if someone dies be like oh fuck they got shot'), and how loud is fear in a fight

cards.mouth: A SIDE QUEST ON THE ROAD
cards.who_plain: A one-eyed man who did a dying woman wrong, at the end of her story
cards.when: you carried a dying woman's words to him and asked nothing for it
cards.where: on the MAP, on the side quest's last card
cards.teaches: A THANK-YOU FOR HELP NOBODY PAID FOR: your law says nobody helps out of kindness and everybody knows it; this line thanks you for exactly that; does it stand in hell, and how does thanks sound

cards.mouth: A JOB GIVER AT THE BOARD
cards.who_plain: A grandmother at the job board
cards.when: you ask what her job is and what it pays
cards.where: in a camp or TOWN, at the board where people offer jobs
cards.expect: My grandson eats at the stew cart
cards.teaches: THE SAME MOUTH AS THE OLD WOMAN YOU STARRED, ANOTHER PERSON: does your star carry ('dark shadows', the ask at the end, 'some batteries', never a number) to a grandmother who is afraid of what is in her grandson's stew
